prompt:
Depot slip (fictional): "Parcel 7731 for Dalia Wren weighs 4 kg and goes to Port Ashby."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys: "recipient" (string), "parcel_id" (number), "weight_kg" (number), "destination" (string). No other keys and no extra text.

Sentence (fictional): "At the Hollin Fair, Brann played the fiddle, then the ocarina, and finished on the tambour."
Reply with ONLY a JSON array of exactly 3 strings: the three instruments in the order they were played, in lowercase. No object, no keys, no extra text.

Notice (fictional): "Tindle Museum is open on Mondays. There is no cafe in the building."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys: "name" (string), "open_monday" (JSON boolean true or false, not a string), "has_cafe" (JSON boolean true or false, not a string). No other keys and no extra text.

Harbor log (fictional): "The cutter Pelican Drift is commanded by Captain Orla Venn."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly two keys: "ship" (string, the ship's name) and "captain" (an object with exactly the keys "first" and "last", holding the captain's first name and last name). No other keys and no extra text.

Recipe card (fictional): "Barley stew. Serves 6. Simmer for 45 minutes in a 3 litre pot."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys: "dish" (string, lowercase), "serves" (number), "minutes" (number, the simmering time). No other keys and no extra text.

Dart game (fictional): Kessa threw four darts and scored 12, then 7, then 19, then 3, in that order.
Reply with ONLY a JSON array of exactly 4 numbers: the four scores in the order thrown. Numbers must not be in quotes. No keys, no extra text.

Timetable note (fictional): "Bramholt station has 3 platforms."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys: "station" (string, the station name written in UPPERCASE letters) and "platforms" (number). No other keys and no extra text.

Locker receipt (fictional): "Locker code 0427, shelf 9, fee 3.50 crowns."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:
"code": the locker code as a STRING, keeping the leading zero
"shelf": the shelf as a number
"fee": the fee as a number (not a string, no currency word)
No other keys and no extra text.

Clinic form (fictional): "Patient name: Ivo Marsh. Phone: not provided. Allergies: none listed."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:
"name": string
"phone": the phone number as a string, or JSON null if it is not provided
"allergies": a JSON array of strings, empty if there are none
No other keys and no extra text.

Shelter list (fictional): Nib the ferret is 2 years old; Sorrel the goat is 7 years old; Quince the parrot is 11 years old.
Reply with ONLY a JSON array of exactly 3 objects, in the order listed. Each object has exactly two keys: "name" (string) and "age" (number). Do not include the kind of animal. No extra text.

Town note (fictional): "Wexcombe has four streets: Tanner Row, Ash Lane, Miller Gate, Dove Street."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly two keys: "town" (string) and "streets" (a JSON array of the four street names sorted alphabetically from A to Z, spelled exactly as given). No other keys and no extra text.

Flyer (fictional): "Kite Workshop in room 2B on floor 2. 40 seats."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object shaped exactly like this example for different data:
{"event": {"title": "Clay Class", "room": {"floor": 5, "label": "5A"}}, "seats": 12}
Use the flyer's values. "floor" and "seats" are numbers, "title" and "label" are strings. No other keys and no extra text.

Poster (fictional): "Lantern Night will be held on 9 March 2041."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly two keys: "festival" (string) and "date" (an object with exactly the keys "year", "month", "day", all numbers; write the month as its number, where January is 1). No other keys and no extra text.

Memo (fictional): "Orchard Committee: room 4, time 09:30. Correction: the room is now room 9; the time is unchanged."
Reply with ONLY one JSON object describing the meeting AFTER the correction, with exactly these keys: "committee" (string, the committee's full two-word name as written in the memo), "room" (number), "time" (string in the form HH:MM). No other keys and no extra text.

Stockroom (fictional), item and units: rope 14, lamp 3, tarp 8, flare 2, hook 21, net 4.
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:
"low_stock": a JSON array of the item names with fewer than 5 units, in the order listed above
"low_count": how many items are in that array (number)
"total_units": the sum of the units of ALL six items (number)
No other keys and no extra text.

Quiz night sign-up (fictional), in order: Ansel (red team), Birdie (blue team), Corin (blue team), Dessa (red team), Eamon (blue team).
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly two keys, "red" and "blue". Each value is a JSON array of the names on that team, in sign-up order. Every name must appear exactly once. No other keys and no extra text.

Sled race times in seconds (fictional): Halvard 52, Mirrin 47, Osk 61, Petra 55. The lowest time is the fastest.
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:
"fastest": the fastest racer's name in all lowercase
"slowest": the slowest racer's name in ALL UPPERCASE
"gap": slowest time minus fastest time (number)
No other keys and no extra text.

Bakery board (fictional): plum tart 9, rye roll 2, fig cake 14, oat bar 5.
Reply with ONLY a JSON array of exactly 4 objects, sorted from the CHEAPEST to the most expensive. Each object has exactly two keys: "item" (string, as written) and "price" (number). No extra text.

Rowing club record (fictional): Marlo won 3 medals, Tess won 5 medals, Ugo won 2 medals.
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly four keys: one key per rower, which is the rower's name in lowercase, with that rower's medal count as a number; and the key "total" with the sum of all medals as a number. Shape example for other data: {"ada": 1, "bo": 4, "total": 5}. No other keys and no extra text.

Outfitter order (fictional): compass 18 coins, map case 7 coins, boots 31 coins. The buyer's budget is 50 coins.
Reply with ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:
"total": the sum of the three prices (number)
"within_budget": JSON boolean, true if the total is less than or equal to the budget, otherwise false
"priciest": the name of the most expensive item (string)
No other keys and no extra text.

Coach timetable (fictional), travel time to each stop: Fenwater 1 h 20 min, Colby Rise 45 min, Stag Moor 2 h 5 min.
Reply with ONLY a JSON array of exactly 3 objects, in the order listed. Each object has exactly two keys: "stop" (string) and "minutes" (the travel time converted to total minutes, as a number; 1 h is 60 min). No extra text.
negative: [{"stop": "Fenwater", "minutes": "1 h 20 min"}, {"stop": "Colby Rise", "minutes": "45 min"}, {"stop": "Stag Moor", "minutes": "2 h 5 min"}]
